messages:
alex: taking handoff for 01:00-09:00 PT. Primary=alex, Secondary=sara. I'm in transit but online via phone. Quick summary: we have a recurring non-blocking spike in tokenstore write latency and a prefetch worker backlog causing increased end-to-end tail latency for some embeddings requests. No P1 customer-facing outage right now, but p99 latency for embeddings has slipped ~400ms.

incident-bot: ALERT: tokenstore.write.latency p95 > 250ms (triggered 4 times in last 30m).

sara: ack. saw the alert. I left a quick runbook note under /runbooks/tokenstore-write (link: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/tokenstore-write). Mitigations in progress: shifting a small subset of traffic to prim-sec fallback pool and increasing tokenstore client retries backoff.

jon: adding context — around 23:40 local a deploy to prefetch-service went out with a change to batch sizing. That increased IO contended windows on a few hosts. I rolled back the batch change at 00:10 which reduced steady-state but we still see spikes under short load bursts.

miguel: metrics: KV eviction rate is normal, disk util on affected nodes peaked at 78% for ~5m during the spike. CPU was fine. Attaching a quick sampling of logs:
```
2026-03-15T00:58:12Z prefetch ERROR write timeout tokenstore id=tx-9f4a
2026-03-15T01:01:03Z prefetch WARN retrying batch size=128 -> 64
```

alex: current mitigations applied before handoff: 1) traffic steering for 5% of embeddings to secondary tokenstore replica (warm). 2) temporarily reduced prefetch batch size via featureflag (ff_prefetch_batch=64). 3) increased client retry jitter to smooth bursts.

lisa: customer ops note — two customers (acme-corp, synthai) have reported intermittent 500s on a small fraction of embedding calls in the last 2 hours. Support triage says impact is <0.5% of their traffic and not affecting core text generation. I updated the support ticket with the steering mitigation.

sara: playbook pointers for night: - If tokenstore p95 > 500ms and customer 500s > 1%, escalate to oncall@ (pager). - If eviction rate > 200/s, paging to eng-sre. - Otherwise continue traffic steering + rolling restart on the 3 affected prefetch hosts (jon volunteered to coordinate).

jon: I queued rolling restart; will do one node at a time, notify here before each. ETA 35m for the full cycle. Will monitor p99s between restarts.

miguel: note about cost: steering to secondary increases tokenstore egress by ~8% for those requests. Fine short-term but call it out if we hold longer than 2h.

alex: coverage gaps: I'm primary but will be on a 20-minute commute starting 01:25 — sara will be primary in that window and i'll be reachable by phone. If anything escalates to customer-impacting (>1% 500s) escalate immediately.

sara: noted. I'll take over at 01:25. My steps if escalation: 1) promote secondary pool (full reroute) via internal tool `/reroute promote secondary tokenstore` 2) open bridge and invite eng-runtime + eng-ml. 3) prepare incident template (I have one at https://confluence.internal/incidents/templates/latency).

alex: open questions for next shift: - Can we confirm whether the prefetch rollback fully reverted all batch-size changes? jon responded yes but please validate config on each host. - Need a follow-up postmortem candidate: if we see recurrence after 3rd restart, treat this as candidate.

incident-bot: NOTE: scheduled warmfix window from 02:00-02:15 for rolling restarts (initiated by jon).

jon: starting first restart in 5m. Will post status after each node: `node1 -> node2 -> node3` sequence.

lisa: I've told support to delay proactive customer notifications unless impact crosses 1%. Will keep tickets updated. :thumbsup:

sara: I'll keep a watch dashboard pinned. If p99 remains > 800ms for more than 10m after a restart, escalate.

alex: leaving this handoff note pinned: ongoing mitigations list, runbook links, primary/secondary, and expected restart window. Back to commute, ping me if it starts to look like P1. :eyes:
